requirements.requirement: Export /srv/nfs/shared from node1 and mount it at /mnt/shared on node2.
requirements.summary: node1 actively exports the requested path to node2, while node2 has it mounted read-write over NFSv4. Final checks after both node restarts show the export, mount, and supporting services recovered and remained operational.

requirements.requirement: Create the shared dataops identity with UID and GID 4500 on both systems, and make the shared directory dataops:dataops with mode 2770.
requirements.summary: Both nodes directly report dataops as UID/GID 4500. The server directory and its client-mounted view both report ownership 4500:4500 and mode 2770, including after restarts.

requirements.requirement: Ensure files created from either system retain consistent ownership and permissions across the share.
requirements.summary: Files created as dataops on node1 and node2 were read successfully from the opposite node and consistently reported UID/GID 4500:4500 with mode 660. A further end-to-end write and read succeeded after both nodes had restarted.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Initial and final observations consistently show Alpine 3.23.3 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts on both nodes. The NFS software was installed through Alpine's native package manager and was operational after reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart observation, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered service, identity, data, permissions, and cross-node access.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Package installation, identity and directory creation, export and mount configuration, service enablement, bounded test-file creation, and node restarts all had clear roles as prerequisites, implementation, direct final evidence, or the mandatory restart protocol. The failed initial node2 check stopped at a permission-denied read and provides no evidence of mutation. Retained NFS test files were bounded evidence used to demonstrate bidirectional behavior and recovery. Added NFS/RPC listeners and runtime package-state changes are expected consequences of the required active NFS service; no new temporary-file residue was observed.
